svg.title: Grad-CAM step by step
svg.desc: Feature maps and their gradients are pooled into channel weights, combined, rectified, normalised and overlaid on the image with the JET colormap.
svg.text: Toy numbers on a 7×7 grid (the EfficientNetB3 top_conv resolution) with 4 of the 1536 channels; the overlay is produced by the real overlay_heatmap.

g.text: • A positive αₖ means "more of channel k raises the class score"; A³ gets a negative α, so skin is suppressed.
• ReLU keeps only evidence for the class; dividing by the maximum maps the result to [0, 1].
• The app computes the map on the first selected model only, for the class chosen
by the (possibly ensembled) prediction, and stores it as heatmaps/<id>_heatmap.npy.
• The divisor is the maximum of the map before ReLU and has no epsilon: if it is 0 the map becomes NaN,
if it is negative the map is all zeros.
